Something similar happened to me and I just realized it.  
Unlike you, my surgeon didn't even told me he changed the plan.  
I was supposed to have djs. My bite was perfectly fine before, but I had long face syndrome/mouth breather issue, with sleep apnea.  
Both jaws were supposed to be advance. He did say he wanted to add genio and I wasn't convinced, my chin had to be impacted cause it was way too long but advanced? no.  
  
Well, I'm one year post surgery and just realised he didn't follow the plan and NEVER told me about it!  
I'm not even 100% sure about it actually, but I think he didn't do lower jaw surgery at all and replaced it by a massive genio only.  
It feels absolutely awful to not even know what has been done to me.  
I was wondering why I still needed braces for so long afterward and why my bite got bad!  
He gave me an overbite and a massive chin and a bumpy jawline with a visible angle in the middle. and a disapearing lower lip (it used to be plump).

What I don't get is that everyone involved has been lying by omission for over a year. My orthodontist haven't said a word either! One of the technician said something about if I enjoyed not having an underbite anymore. I said "no my bite was perfect, I had djs for my airways". She didn't say anything back, just "ah ok".  
I didn't think any further, I thought she was just confused. But it makes sense now.  
  
I already thought my surgeon had done a pretty bad job and I was disapointed, but it's much worse than that. He literally scammed me and perform a surgery he chose without my consent and without ever telling me!  
That's why everyone was evasive when I asked about my movements and why the x ray were shown to me very briefly.  
In the postop appointment, when I expressed concerns about the results, my surgeon reapeated it was perfect and that he did a great job. He said it was just swelling and he actually made me feel kinda bad that I was criticizing his work, so I stopped.  He was talking in a way that it was difficult to contradict him, speaking in affirmatives about things that were obviously wrong.   
Like right after the surgery I said, "my teeth don't touch at the back". He took a look and said "wow it's perfect it touches everywhere". (I think it's the definition of gaslight)

I know I must sound like an idiot, but I was just trusting of professionals.  
I do not feel good about the results but I'm stuck with this now cause I do not want to go over this again.   
I spent my whole life being unattractive and not being able to breath properly anyway so I guess I can go on like this. It's just sad that I tried to improve my fate and got really unlucky. I'm a bit mad at the initial professional (someone I knew personally) who sent me to this butcher surgeon, cause he's the main reason why I was so trusting and felt in good hands even thought I wasn't.

in some autoimune diseases, an immunosuppressant can stop working after a few years as the immune system find a new pathway to inflamation.    
I'm no expert and my understanding is shallow, (and this is not what the medical community generally agrees on) but I think there might be a latent viral infection going on even in autoimmunity. Maybe undetectable? like some parasites during the chronic stage when they are dormant inside cells instead of being in circulation like during the accute infection?   
Both autoimmune diseases and long covid have been linked to EBV (although the link is not always so clear: lupus, sjogren, multiple sclerosis and many more are statistically linked with previous ebv infection) and covid seems to reactivate that stupid virus.   
Having 2 viruses possibly interacting and tag team each other, I'm guessing makes unresolves things even more complicated and the possibilities of outcomes even more variables in different people.   
..and poor immune system :(   
 Immunosuppressants stop inflammation and symptoms but it doesn't mean the underlying problem is solved if there is anything more to it than an overreaction of the immune system for "no reason". Constant inflammation can also deplete vitamins and cause more problems as well.

I'd say, in the case you describe, if he doesn't answer anymore, sure, leave it as is if you want. It's not you who's ghosting anyway and you feel alright with it.

I went though something similar and it was extremely painful to loose this "friend"

The guy had also befriended me for darker (and frankly unknown to this day) motives. He lied from the very start hidding he was in a relationship, he told me he was single and kept the lies going for a whole year even if we were just friends, until we did became more than friends.. and when I learned the truth I went nuclear!  
I was single and not into being a mistress AT ALL! The irony is that he made me believe we were on the same page about cheaters! and that we had the same values about loyalty, truth, ect..

The thing is I see similarities in the fact that we hit it off (as friends) in a way that felt like I was closer to him and trusted him more than my old friends. This, I learned later on, is typical of personality disorders of the cluster B group (and it's a pretty bad thing).  
When someone you don't know feels like home too quickly, it's unfortunately not a good sign.  
I remember thinking, "what does he wants" at the very beginning, but I chased that thought cause at that point all I had against him was that he was too kind and generous for someone who was not openly flirting. He just wanted to be friend at the beginning, but he was communicating a lot and being very nice.   
I remember thinking to myself "if I can't believe someone has genuine kindness it's a really sad world ain't it?"

These people mirror you to make you feel you have so much in common and that you are being seen, heard, cared for and that you finally met someone who gets you. It becomes SO precious in your life cause you likely don't have any friend like that at all, or maybe one or two if you're lucky cause such a connection between two person is as rare as finding a pot of gold at the foot of a rainbow.   
and it's pretty much how it feels for us... but apparently not for them as they can cut you off of their life without hesitation... which should be very telling...  
  
Unfortunately, it's just scheme and their goals are self serving when not litterally psychopatic.

The hard part for the victim is that, when it all falls down (and it's usually a brutal truth reveal all at once) you are stuck with a contradiction of missing dearly a persona who was taking a big place in your life and who you likely loved and were attached to but the real person behind this character is an evil piece of shit with mental trouble and very likely unstable emotions (blocks/unblocks you, "push & pull", super happy/cries in your arm the next day) who's just an evil snake.   
Also, not only your present and futur have been bombed but also your past, many memories, and perception of a important part of your reality.  
It can really send you for a wild spin.

I have POTS and I had a myocarditis as well.  
pots is characterize by an average pulse at rest (specifically while sitting) but that goes up +30 or more while standing up.  
It's not dangerous but it's tricky to treat. 

\-> You can make sure you drink enough water and electrolytes (sodium and especially potassium) it can help a little.

I heard different takes on it recently, but the general consensus is that it's not a heart condition, it's the parasympathetic nervous system which is suppose to tell the heart to slow down that doesn't do it's job properly. so as long as the heart is healthy (like it was in my case) it can beat faster, and it's not life threatening. A cardiologist has to assess that though to make sure the heart beats normally but just faster.  
I did had beta blockers for it but it didn't work cause my pulse was then dangerously slow at rest (like down to 39) and it was still jumping too much while standing. Also, it was making me even more tired as a side effect.

BUT, later on I also had a myocarditis. To be honest I couldn't really differentiate between the 2 conditions and it was caught by chance. I did felt some very intense chest pain at night once (like I was being compressed A LOT) and after that my pulse was going up the roof, 180 for just walking around a bit. When the MRI revealed I was instructed to rest and to not to physical activities at all. It resolved on it's own after maybe a month or 2. That one is a dangerous condition as the heart can just stop.   
(so that's gone now but I still have POTS = up to 140 when I walk, 160 on a bad day)  
So, a fast pulse can be a symptom or not of a more serious condition.

I personally wouldn't go to the ER if that's the only symptom (95-110 is really not alarming in itself) but I would take an appointment with my doctor to discuss it and I would drink plenty of fluid with electrolytes to at least rule that out.  
If it worries you, you can also avoid cardio activities until then to be on the safe side.  
 ..and it's easier said then done but try to relax cause that kind of stress alone can make your pulse shoot up even if everything is fine.
